title: What if the Moon had Earth's gravity?
style: stylized low-poly 3D animation, simple geometric shapes, flat matte colors, first-person POV at eye level, as if the viewer is standing in the scene, gentle handheld camera, simple low-poly people, deep navy night tones with warm amber light accents, soft lighting, vertical 9:16, no text, no logos, no flags, no watermarks
description: What if the Moon pulled as hard as Earth? Monster tides, a double planet, and a Moon nobody could leave. Real science, imagined.

sources.claim: Moon: surface gravity 1.62 m/s2, radius 1,737 km, mass 0.0735e24 kg, escape velocity 2.38 km/s, mean distance 384,400 km
Earth: surface gravity 9.80 m/s2, mass 5.97e24 kg
Six times the mass (calculation): at the same radius, g scales with mass, so 9.80 / 1.62 = 6.05x the Moon's mass
Tide-generating force scales with the Moon's mass, so the lunar tide gets about 6x stronger (estimate; local tides vary)
Today the Earth-Moon barycenter sits about 4,700 km from Earth's center, inside the planet
New barycenter (calculation): 384,400 km x 0.444 / (5.972 + 0.444) = about 26,600 km from Earth's center, outside Earth (radius 6,371 km)
New escape velocity (calculation): 2.38 km/s x sqrt(6.05) = about 5.9 km/s, nearly 2.5x today and above Mars (5.03 km/s)
Apollo LM ascent engine: about 15,500 N of thrust
LM ascent stage fueled: about 4,800 kg (2,180 kg dry + 2,639 kg propellant); at 9.8 m/s2 it weighs about 47,000 N, three times the engine's thrust (calculation)
SPECULATION: a Moon with escape velocity above Mars's could hold some gas; whether it would form an atmosphere is not established
Tides brake Earth's spin and lengthen the day; a heavier Moon brakes faster (qualitative)
Pluto and Charon are mutually tidally locked: the same faces always point at each other

motion_style: stylized low-poly 3D animation, first-person POV at eye level

scenes.prompt: Standing on a harbor wall at night looking down at the sea drained far out, little boats lying tilted on wet mud, a huge glowing full Moon ahead
scenes.motion: slow handheld push forward toward the railing, moonlight glinting on the wet faceted mud, lamp lights flickering softly, tiny people on the harbor wall leaning over to look
scenes.on_screen: What if the Moon had Earth's gravity?

scenes.prompt: Walking along a quiet seaside promenade at night, a few people strolling ahead, looking up at an ordinary full Moon over calm dark water
scenes.motion: slow walk forward along the promenade, people strolling ahead, gentle waves rolling in, moonlight shimmering on the water, camera tilting slightly up toward the Moon
scenes.narration: Tonight, nothing looks different. Same Moon. Same size. Same glow.

scenes.prompt: Looking into a backyard telescope eyepiece at night, the full Moon filling the view, craters as simple flat facets
scenes.motion: very slow drift as the eye settles on the eyepiece, the faceted lunar surface sharpening into focus, faint shimmer of air
scenes.narration: But to pull like Earth, something that small needs six times its mass.

scenes.prompt: Standing on a beach at dawn, the waterline retreated far out ahead, exposed seabed with rocks and seaweed, people walking out onto it
scenes.motion: slow walk forward onto the wet exposed seabed, the last water draining away into the distance, people ahead walking out and pointing, puddles glinting
scenes.narration: Six hours later, the sea pulls back. The Moon now tugs the oceans six times harder.

scenes.prompt: Standing on the steps of a shop in a small coastal town, seawater flowing calmly into the street below, knee deep around parked cars
scenes.motion: camera holds on the steps, then tilts down as seawater flows steadily up the street, rising around the car wheels, ripples spreading, shop lights reflecting on the water
scenes.narration: Then the tide returns. Not up the beach. Into the streets. Twice a day.

scenes.prompt: Standing in a dim museum hall in front of a cutaway model of Earth, a small glowing amber point deep inside the planet
scenes.motion: slow push in toward the cutaway Earth model, the amber point deep inside pulsing gently
scenes.narration: Today, Earth and Moon circle a point inside our planet, 4,700 kilometers from its center.

scenes.prompt: Earth and the Moon in space, both slowly circling an empty glowing point between them
scenes.style: stylized low-poly 3D animation, simple geometric shapes, flat matte colors, deep navy space with warm amber light accents, simple stars, soft lighting, slow orbital camera, vertical 9:16, no text, no logos, no watermarks
scenes.motion: Earth and Moon slowly orbit together around the glowing empty point between them, camera slowly circling the pair
scenes.motion_style: stylized low-poly 3D animation, slow orbital camera
scenes.narration: Now that point sits 26,000 kilometers out, in empty space. Earth swings around it every month. We're a double planet.

scenes.prompt: Standing behind a fence across a field at night, a rocket on a launch pad ahead with floodlights and rising steam
scenes.motion: steam billowing around the rocket, floodlights flaring, handheld camera behind the fence slowly tilting up to the top of the rocket
scenes.narration: Going back there gets brutal. To escape the Moon, a rocket needs nearly two and a half times the speed.

scenes.prompt: Standing in a quiet museum hall looking up at a gold-foil lunar lander model
scenes.motion: slow tilt up the lander from its legs to its top, dust motes floating in the museum light
scenes.narration: The lander that brought Apollo home? Its engine couldn't even lift its own weight.

scenes.prompt: Standing on the lunar surface at sunrise, gray faceted plains and craters ahead, a thin faint blue haze along the horizon, Earth low in a black sky
scenes.motion: slow walk forward across the faceted lunar plain, fine dust lifting at each step, the thin blue haze glowing on the horizon as the Sun rises
scenes.narration: With that grip, the Moon could hold on to gas better than Mars. Maybe, one day, a thin sky.

scenes.prompt: Earth seen from space with its night side facing away from a motionless Moon, city lights only on the far side
scenes.style: stylized low-poly 3D animation, simple geometric shapes, flat matte colors, deep navy space with warm amber light accents, simple stars, soft lighting, slow orbital camera, vertical 9:16, no text, no logos, no watermarks
scenes.motion: slow orbit around Earth with the Moon fixed in place, the line between day and night creeping across the planet
scenes.motion_style: stylized low-poly 3D animation, slow orbital camera
scenes.narration: Given time, tides lock Earth and Moon face to face, like Pluto and Charon. Half the world never sees it again.

scenes.prompt: Standing on the same seaside promenade from the opening at night, looking up at an ordinary full Moon over calm water
scenes.motion: standing still on the promenade, a single person ahead stops and looks up at the Moon, gentle waves, camera slowly tilting up toward the Moon
scenes.narration: And the strangest part? From your window, the Moon would look exactly the same. What should I imagine next?
